root_cause.text: In mm/vmalloc.c, vrealloc_node_align_noprof() used old_size as the memcpy length on the need_realloc path after allocating a new buffer of only size bytes, so shrinking reallocations with forced reallocation overflowed the new vmalloc buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `memcpy(n, p, old_size);` to `memcpy(n, p, min(size, old_size));`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that when `size < old_size` on the `need_realloc` path, a new object of `size` bytes was allocated and then `old_size` bytes were copied into it, causing an out-of-bounds write.

intent_record.intent_summary: Limit vrealloc_node_align_noprof() copies to the smaller of the old and new sizes to avoid overflow when shrinking allocations.
intent_record.what: The memcpy call inside vrealloc_node_align_noprof() was changed from copying old_size bytes from p to n to copying min(size, old_size) bytes instead.
intent_record.how: This prevents copying more bytes than the newly allocated buffer size when reallocating to a smaller size, avoiding a potential buffer overflow while still preserving as much existing data as fits in the new allocation.

grouping_result.intent: Limit vrealloc_node_align_noprof() copies to the smaller of the old and new sizes to avoid overflow when shrinking allocations.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause in vrealloc_node_align_noprof() by capping the memcpy length to the minimum of old and new sizes, preventing overflow during shrinking reallocations when a new smaller vmalloc buffer is allocated.

candidates.rationale: This copies old_size bytes into the newly allocated buffer n even on shrinking reallocations where n was allocated with only size bytes, directly causing the overflow described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: On the forced reallocation path in vrealloc_node_align_noprof(), this copies old_size bytes from the old allocation into the new buffer n, even when n was newly allocated with only size bytes during a shrinking reallocation. That mismatch causes the vmalloc buffer overflow described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it fully shows the reallocation decision and copy length logic. The root cause described is copying `old_size` bytes into a newly allocated buffer of only `size` bytes on a forced reallocation shrink path. That vulnerable construct is not present here. Instead, the code explicitly avoids reallocating when shrinking: `if (size <= old_size) { ... return (void *)p; }`. So for shrink requests, it returns the original allocation and optionally zeroes the spare tail with `memset((void *)p + size, 0, old_size - size);`. A new buffer is only allocated on the grow path: `n = __vmalloc_noprof(size, flags);` after the `size <= old_size` early return, which implies `size > old_size` at that point. Therefore the subsequent `memcpy(n, p, old_size);` copies at most the old size into a buffer that is larger than old_size, which is safe. Thus the vulnerable shrink-with-reallocation overflow condition does not exist in this function, and the relevant fix/avoidance is already present.
